arxiv-2011-13854.creator: Marvin M. Müller, Miriam Kosik, Marta Pelc, Garnett W. Bryant, Andrés Ayuela, Carsten Rockstuhl, Karolina Słowik
arxiv-2011-13854.description: Abstract Plasmonic nanostructures attract tremendous attention as they confine electromagnetic fields well below the diffraction limit while simultaneously sustaining extreme local field enhancements. To fully exploit these properties, the identification and classification of resonances in such nanostructures is crucial. Recently, a novel figure of merit for resonance classification has been proposed Müller et al.

arxiv-2112-09190.title: Monitoring crop phenology with street-level imagery using computer vision Journal: Submitted to Computers and Electronics in Agriculture
arxiv-2112-09190.creator: Raphaël d’Andrimont, 1,∗ Momchil Yordanov 1,∗ Laura Martinez-Sanchez 1 Marijn van der Velde 1
arxiv-2112-09190.description: Abstract Street-level imagery holds a significant potential to scale-up in-situ data collection. This is enabled by combining the use of cheap high quality cameras with recent advances in deep learning compute solutions to derive relevant thematic information. We present a framework to collect and extract crop type and phenological information from street level imagery using computer vision.

arxiv-2302-11925.title: Practical study of optical stellar interferometry
arxiv-2302-11925.creator: P. Rodríguez-Ovalle, A. Mendi-Martos, A .Angulo-Manzanas, I. Reyes-Rodríguez, M.Pérez-Arrieta, M. A. Illarramendi, A. Sánchez-Lavega
arxiv-2302-11925.description: Abstract We present a technique to observe stellar inteferograms, as well as the detailed analysis of those created by three bright stars: Betelgeuse, Rigel, and Sirius. It is shown that the atmospheric turbulence is responsible for the reduction of the long-exposure fringe visibility of the obtained interference patterns.

arxiv-2510-20768.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Austin Jia 1 , Avaneesh Ramesh 1 , Zain Shamsi, Daniel Zhang, and Alex Liu. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as the dominant architectural pattern to operationalize Large Language Model (LLM) usage in Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) systems. However, this design is susceptible to poisoning attacks, and previously proposed defenses can fail for CTI contexts as cyber threat information is often completely new for emerging attacks and sophisticated threat actors can mimic legitimate formats, terminology, and stylistic conventions.

pmc-11680428.description: Anatoxin-a (ATX-a) is a cyanotoxin whose toxicological profile has been underinvestigated in comparison to other cyanotoxins such as microcystins (MCs) or cylindrospermopsin (CYN). pmc-13173928.title: Flavin-dependent monooxygenases as versatile biocatalysts in biomanufacturing: mechanisms, engineering, and applications
pmc-13173928.creator: Yong Li, Ling Zhao, Xin Pu, Biao Geng, Wei Liu, Jie Gao, Xiaowei Peng, Yejun Han
pmc-13173928.description: Flavin-dependent monooxygenases (FMOs) are versatile oxidative biocatalysts that catalyze a wide array of oxygenation reactions, such as hydroxylation, epoxidation, Baeyer–Villiger oxidation, and halogenation. These enzymes utilize flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD) or flavin mononucleotide (FMN) as cofactors to mediate selective incorporation of oxygen into diverse substrates.

pmc-13215613.title: Dual-channel graph learning reveals similarity and complementarity in protein-protein interaction networks
pmc-13215613.creator: Tao Tang, Taiguang Shen, Weizhuo Li, Yangyang Chen, Sisi Yuan, Yuansheng Liu, Xinyu Yang, Xiao Luo
pmc-13215613.description: Protein-protein interactions (PPIs) are governed by two fundamental interfacial mechanisms: similarity-driven, often involving symmetric structural motifs, and complementarity-driven, arising from geometric and physicochemical matching between binding surfaces. Despite their biological significance, computational models have largely overlooked the coexistence and interplay of these twofold interaction modes.

pmc-13391360.title: Acquired genetic and cell-state changes in IDH-mutant glioma progression
pmc-13391360.creator: Kevin C. Johnson, Avishay Spitzer, Frederick S. Varn, Masashi Nomura, Luciano Garofano, Tamrin Chowdhury, Anuja Lipsa, Linbin Zhang, Ester Calvo Fernández, Tanyeri Barak, A. Gulhan Ercan-Sencicek, Ayse Buket Peksen, Kevin J. Anderson, C. Mircea S. Tesileanu, Samirkumar B. Amin, Emre Kocakavuk, Dache
pmc-13391360.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Gliomas with mutant isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) are malignant brain tumours that typically arise in early to mid-adulthood and nearly always recur following treatment1,2. However, the genetic and cellular-state changes that drive IDH-mutant glioma progression under treatment remain incompletely understood. Here we integrated single-nucleus transcriptomic profiles, chromatin accessibility profiles and bulk DNA and RNA sequencing from 75 temporally separated gliomas across 35 patients comprising both the oligodendroglioma and astrocytoma IDH-mutant glioma tumour types.

pmc-7619508.title: Neurochemical drivers of effort: The roles of dopamine and beyond in physical and cognitive exertion
pmc-7619508.creator: Eva Periche-Tomas, Masud Husain, Matthew A.J. Apps, Simon Little, Catherine J. Harmer
pmc-7619508.description: Motivation depends on the ability to evaluate whether potential rewards are worth the effort required to obtain them. Disruptions in this process give rise to debilitating motivational syndromes such as apathy and anhedonia, which are prominent across neurological and psychiatric disorders, including depression and Parkinson’s disease.
